source_text: caenosa confugerim, exhorreas consequi atque perimere: quia videlicet partes disputationis tuae, quibus atterendus vel perimendus sum, quoniam de pudendis loqui cogeris, velut quidam aedituus pudor tuus a verborum libertate submovit
pass_a_gloss: Caenosa confugerim, exhorreas consequi and perimere: because namely partes disputationis your, to-whom atterendus or perimendus sum, quoniam about/from pudendis loqui cogeris, as-if a-certain aedituus modesty your from verborum by-freedom submovit.

lemmas.lexica: LS libertas; Blaise moral freedom to will or refuse

pass_b_english: [His] position is a bedbug: alive it causes trouble, and crushed it gives off a stench.
[I am] ashamed to crush him by defeating him.
As though defeated, [he has] fled to filthy places, and [I] recoil from following and killing him.
Because [I am] forced to speak about the sexual organs, [my] modesty, like a temple keeper, has excluded from free expression the parts of [my] argument that would crush or destroy him.

choices.why: Freedom to abstain is required for will and sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
